To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
strategic grazing management can be effective in reducing upland bare ground on New Mexico midgrass prairies and increasing vegetative cover in riparian zones.
strategic grazing management (SGM) increased riparian vegetation cover and decreased bare ground in midgrass prairie rangeland pastured with cattle.

strategic management of livestock grazing on New Mexico mid-grass prairie rangelands increased vegetative cover on upland and riparian areas compared to continuous stocking, and that the cover of bare ground on strategically managed pastures was comparable to pastures that had been rested from grazing for at least three years.

strategic management of livestock grazing on the ranch scale is effective in reducing upland bare ground, increasing riparian vegetative ground cover, and improving range condition.

strategic management of rangeland livestock production can be used to improve land cover and reduce the impacts of grazing on riparian ecosystems.

strategically managed ranches can be as effective as pastures rested for three years or more in improving upland bare ground cover and riparian cover.
strategically managed ranches can provide similar or better vegetative cover and range condition than pastures rested from livestock use for three or more consecutive years.
